svg.title: v11 → v12: realize the M=128 GEMM on Blackwell tcgen05 tensor cores
svg.desc: A left-to-right lever diagram, four boxes. Box 1 (orange, the wall): v11 ran the right SHAPE on the wrong ENGINE — a warp-per-head CUDA-core GEMV that packs M=128 as 16 blocks x 8 warps, NOT one tensor-core GEMM (no wmma/mma/tcgen05 tokens in source). Measured per-CTA-bound: 0.75 TFLOP/s achieved (under 1 percent of either compute peak), %HBM about zero flat to N_k=2M past a 5.1x L2 overflow. On B300 it runs about 4x SLOWER than torch dense-MQA (vs_sdpa 0.23 to 0.29x at 576/512), because tuned cuBLAS batched-GEMV beats a hand-written CUDA-core GEMV. Box 2 (blue, the lever): that about-4x cuBLAS gap is the empirical proof the M=128 packed GEMM is a real, tensor-core-friendly GEMM and the CUDA-core default is the wrong tool. Box 3 (green, the build): v12 forks CUTLASS example 77 (2-SM tcgen05), Arm 1 = FP8 MMA at the M>=64 gate, then Arm 2 = native NVFP4 at the M>=128 gate — native low-precision COMPUTE, not dequant-to-FP16. Pure roofline predicts a compute-flip past the B300 FP16-TC ridge of 312.5: MLA fp16 AI 234.8 (0.75x, HBM knife-edge), fp8 AI 469.7 (1.50x, MMA), nvfp4 AI 835.0 (2.67x, deep MMA). Box 4 (purple, the prize, pre-registered): even with tensor cores, decode at N_q=1 is expected to stay SMEM-bandwidth-bound (the staged latent feeds the MMA), so it will likely NOT reach the FP4 compute peak — the honest counter-prediction. This is the data-motivated next step, not yet measured; it complements, does not beat, FlashMLA/FlashInfer.
svg.text: v11 → v12: realize M=128 on tcgen05 tensor cores
v11 ran the right shape on the wrong engine; v12 moves the packed GEMM onto Blackwell 5th-gen tensor cores.
CUDA-core GEMV, not a TC GEMM.
Data-motivated next step — not yet measured. Complements, doesn't beat, FlashMLA/FlashInfer.
